ask: Go 1.22, standard library only. shardmap.go: generic sharded concurrent map ShardMap[K comparable, V any] with 32 shards, RWMutex per shard, Get/Set/Delete/Range/Len, fnv hashing of the key, and a benchmark plus a concurrent smoke test. write the file.
prose:
Both files are written. Here's what you've got:

`shardmap.go` — the library
- `ShardMap[K, V]` with 32 shards, one `sync.RWMutex` per shard
- FNV-1a 32-bit hash via `fmt.Fprintf(h, "%v", key)` to convert any `comparable` key to bytes without unsafe or a narrower constraint
- `Get` / `Set` / `Delete` take the shard lock only for their own shard, so operations on different shards never block each other
- `Range` locks one shard at a time and respects an early-stop `false` return
- `Len` sums across shards with per-shard read locks — not an atomic snapshot, but consistent per-shard

`shardmap_test.go` — tests and benchmarks
- `TestGetSetDelete` — basic correctness including overwrite and delete
- `TestLen` — 200 inserts then 100 deletes
- `TestRange` / `TestRangeEarlyStop` — full scan and early termination
- `TestConcurrent` — 64 goroutines × 1 000 ops each, mixed reads/writes/deletes, then a final `Range` sanity check; safe to run with `-race`
- `BenchmarkSet` / `BenchmarkGet` — single-threaded baselines
- `BenchmarkSetParallel` / `BenchmarkGetParallel` / `BenchmarkMixedParallel` — GOMAXPROCS-wide parallel runs; the mixed benchmark is 80% reads / 20% writes

Run everything with:
```
go test -race ./...
go test -bench=. -benchmem ./...
```

One thing worth noting: `fmt.Fprintf` for hashing is correct and generic, but it's the slowest path. If you later constrain `K` to `string | int | ...`, a type switch to `h.Write([]byte(k))` or binary encoding will cut shard-selection cost significantly under heavy load.
